references.text: The prophet Micah describes how a man's enemies are his own household members, and that the son dishonors the father, the daughter rises against her mother, and the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law ([ref:Mi 7:6|Micah 7:6]). This is the direct Old Testament background for Jesus' words in Luke 12:53.

In Matthew, Jesus uses almost identical words saying that he has come to set division between father and son, mother and daughter, mother-in-law and daughter-in-law ([ref:Matt 10:35-36|Matthew 10:35-36]). This is the parallel passage to Luke 12:53.

Jesus says that brother will hand over brother to death, and father his child, and children will rise against parents and cause their death ([ref:Matt 10:21|Matthew 10:21]). This expands on the theme of division within families because of faith.

The immediate context shows that Jesus explains he has not come to bring peace, but division, and that a house with five will be divided, three against two and two against three ([ref:Luk 12:51-52|Luke 12:51-52]). Verse 53 specifies this division with particular family relationships.

Jesus warns the disciples that they will be betrayed by parents, siblings, relatives, and friends, and that some of them will be put to death ([ref:Luk 21:16|Luke 21:16]). This confirms the same theme of family division as a result of following Christ.
Division arose among the crowd because of Jesus ([ref:Joh 7:43|John 7:43]). This shows that Jesus' presence and message actually created conflict, just as he predicted in Luke 12:53.
